citation.title: Core and edge toroidal rotation study in JT-60U
citation.authors: M. Yoshida, Y. Sakamoto, M. Honda, Y. Kamada, H. Takenaga, N. Oyama, H. Urano and the JT-60 Team

topic: JT-60U toroidal rotation physics. The study relates core and edge rotation, fits a residual-stress term and examines edge rotation versus the pedestal ion temperature gradient. Rotation and Ti are measured with carbon CXRS.
own_question: How are core and edge Vt related through momentum transport? Can intrinsic rotation be reproduced with a residual-stress term proportional to the momentum diffusivity times the ion pressure gradient?
actual_method_and_evidence: The authors use offline momentum-balance modelling. Diffusivity and convection velocity come from modulated perpendicular-NB transient analysis. They study L–H and H–L transition timescales of about 20 ms and parameter scans. Residual-stress coefficients are fitted per discharge. They report a sawtooth/NTM mode-frequency check of carbon versus bulk rotation. It covers a different device, and a different target (rotation, not temperature nowcasting). There is no BES/ECEI and no estimator.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Carbon CXRS Ti and Vt are impurity-ion measurements. Carbon-versus-main-ion rotation agreement was checked only indirectly, through MHD mode frequencies, in JT-60U.
claim_checks.qualification: This was a JT-60U rotation check. A residual frequency gap of about 0.5–1 kHz remained. It says nothing about the KSTAR CES temperature.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. The source has no nowcasting, no report-arrival timing and no online inputs.
validation_if_relevant: Fits are made per discharge. There is no held-out validation.
forbidden_inferences: That the source validates KSTAR CES labels
That it supports BES/ECEI information content
That the ~20 ms rotation timescale applies to our 10 ms Ti nowcast
That the fitted residual-stress model is established physics
reason_to_include_or_exclude: This is at most an optional background citation on impurity-versus-main-ion CXRS caveats. It is not about causal temperature estimation, so it can likely be omitted.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
